description:
Musicians and music fans, get informed and get inspired with Blue Bear's new Master Artist Series. On Saturday, March 13, the brand new duo Skerdio - i.e., Skerik and Radioactive - joins Blue Bear for an evening of performance, technique discussion and Q&A. It's a unique opportunity to connect with well-established musicians in an intimate setting. All ages are welcome to this event, and advance tickets are highly recommended, as recent Master Artist Series events sold out in advance.

Renowned saxophonist and Bay Area favorite Skerik (Critters Buggin, Dead Kenny G's, Garage a Trois, Syncopated Taint Septet, Roger Waters, Les Claypool) will bring his latest electronics set up that allows him to efficiently change timbres, sounds and directions. He will demonstrate signal path, unity gain and survival in the electronic music world, meaning survival techniques using any sound system found in any club, theater, church or cult headquarters. From microphones to monitors and everything between, mysteries will be unveiled.

Worldwide underground legend emcee and beatboxer Radioactive (New Native, Top Four Flights, New Clear Vission, True World Order, and formerly of Michael Franti and Spearhead), who holds two Australian Gold Records, will teach standard beatboxing, mic rocking, looping, lyric writing and hook making. He'll also explain crowd participation, mic control, stage presence, album concepts, marketing strategies, freestyling and tour expectations.

Random tips for saxophonists, lyricists, beatboxers and musicians of all types will be brought forth. These two creative characters are joining forces for one night only - don't miss it!

description:
Los nadies have created one of the freshest sounds to come out of the Bay Areas Latin
music scene in a long time. Filling a vacuum in Northern California that their southern counterparts
Ozomatli deliver so well in L.A., Los Nadies bring a keen mix of politics, poetry, street party and
musicianship every time they step on to a stage. Their unique blend of rock, nueva trova, South
American folklore and Afro-Latin rhythms follows and expands on the tradition of celebration and
protest put forth by musicians like Silvio Rodríguez, Manu Chao, and Santana.

Front man Juán Cubas vocals, along with José Vergelíns drums, and Francisco Ferrers lead
guitar, serve as the anchor for the band, having played together for over a decade in Bay Area
Latin rock bands like Zudaka and Santero. Multitalented percussionist Garsha Shavankhani brings
an array of Afro-Peruvian, Afro-Cuban and Flamenco experience into the bands cache of rhythmic
arsenal. Along with Cuba, guitarist Mateo Nube composes the bands lyrics and shares in vocal
duties. Bassist Marco Bianchi is the newest addition to the Los nadies family.
Los nadies take their name from a poem/essay by Uruguayan historian Eduardo Galeano decrying
the invisibility cast upon the millions of dispossessed people around the world.
